messages:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] 11:23 UTC Canary health check failing for release r-2026-03-15-11.23 on cluster 'prod-canary'. 5m error rate = 5.6% (threshold 1%). 90th latency increased 2.4x. Links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rl/canary-health

sarah-oncall: saw the page. paging oncall now. any obvious customer-facing impact?

ana-mlinfra: quick check — embedding generation requests to /v1/embeddings show elevated 502s from the canary pool. Root cause unclear yet, but it correlates with the canary rollout at 11:22. Traffic was 12% routed to canary.

mike_release: fyi automated rollback didn't trigger. Canary monitor check interval was 120s and the rollout window is 10m; may have missed threshold transient. initiating manual coordination.

beth_prod: customer impact: CSMs reporting two enterprise customers seeing timeouts for bulk embed jobs. Not panicking but we should roll back quickly.

tim-sre: +1 on rollback. Can we kill the flag for the new model or do a replica swap? What's simpler?

ana-mlinfra: kill-switch feature flag is scoped in LaunchDarkly under flag 'model_v2_switch'. Turning it off will drain new model instances gradually but we should be careful: the flag is a split at the routing layer, not the infra deployment. If we flip it it will stop new traffic but existing sessions may still land on canary.

mike_release: recommendation: manual rollout rollback to previous replicaset on the canary pool, then revert routing percentage to 0 for canary. That ensures no new canary pods get traffic and we restore previous code path. I'll lead the rollback.

sarah-oncall: ok mike, what's the command sequence? Paste everything so we can follow.

mike_release: runbook below — I'll run, calling it out as I do it:

mike_release: ```
# scale down canary replica set to 0 (kube)
kubectl -n prod set image deploy/model-inference model=model:v20260314-previous --record
# or if using helm: helm rollback model-inference 7 --namespace prod
# revert routing percentage (LaunchDarkly) -> set model_v2_switch rollout to 0%
```

mike_release: kicking the kubectl image set now, will post results.

ops-bot: deploy-job 8421 started by mike_release — rolling update on deployment/model-inference namespace=prod

mike_release: kubectl output: "deployment.apps/model-inference image updated". New rollout started. Pod restarts are in progress.

ana-mlinfra: seeing pods terminating in prod-canary, new pods coming up with previous image. Noted some pod evictions at 11:30, but restarts healthy so far.

tim-sre: I'm going to scale the canary service backend weight to 0 at the LB layer to prevent any new connections during the window. Command: `rtrctl set-weight canary-pool 0`

beth_prod: LaunchDarkly updated to 0% for model_v2_switch by mike_release :white_check_mark:

mike_release: lb weight set to 0 by tim-sre. Confirmed no new connections to canary backend in the last 30s.

sarah-oncall: run smoke tests against /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings to validate revert. I'll run them and paste output.

sarah-oncall: ```bash
# basic smoke for text generation
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${INCIDENT_TEST_KEY}' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":5}' | jq .
# embeddings smoke
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${INCIDENT_TEST_KEY}' -d '{"input":"test"}' | jq .
```

sarah-oncall: generation latency 120ms, 200 OK. embeddings 95ms, 200 OK. No 502s in the sample.

ana-mlinfra: metrics: error rate on canary-pool dropped to baseline within 2 minutes after traffic weight hit 0. 90th latency returned to normal window. CPU/mem on previous replicaset stable.

deploy-bot: [INFO] Rollout finished: deployment/model-inference rolled back to image model:v20260314-previous by mike_release at 11:34 UTC.

beth_prod: contacting the two impacted customers with an update and ETA for postmortem. brief message sent.

tim-sre: quick check of logs shows a spike of "invalid kv-cache" errors from the new image between 11:24-11:28 which likely caused request handling to fail under certain batch sizes. pushing logs to the incident timeline.

mike_release: noted — including log snippet for trace id 0a3f...

mike_release: ```
[11:25:12] ERROR model-serving: failed to lookup kv-cache shard: KeyError shard-42
[11:25:13] ERROR model-serving: batch->dispatch failed for request_id=0a3f...
```

sarah-oncall: good rollback verification. Next steps: create an incident page, tag for postmortem, and handoff to ana-mlinfra for root cause analysis. I'll stay on for 15 more minutes then hand to tim-sre for overnight.

ana-mlinfra: I'll own RCA. collecting diffs between model:v20260314-previous and v20260315-canary, and run unit repro locally on matching batch sizes.

tim-sre: I'll monitor the dashboards and be the next oncall handoff. please add runbook links to the incident page and include the kill-switch state in the timeline.

sarah-oncall: adding notes to incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.internal/1932104567 — summary, timeline, customer notices. Marking severity P2.

deploy-bot: [NOTIFICATION] Incident 1932104567 status=resolved_if_no_regressions waiting 30m for regression window.

beth_prod: thanks all. If the embed customers ask for a postmortem copy asap, send to me and I'll coordinate comms.

mike_release: leaving final logs and helm diff in the incident doc. handoff to tim-sre in 10. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: paging note — @tim-sre now on-duty for follow-up.

sarah-oncall: closing the coordination thread here. If we see any regressions during the 30m window we reopen. great quick work everyone. :white_check_mark:
